So that organ is the SIS or the security service. All my further questions related to the security service, and as far as I understood it, the witness answers without doubt referred to the security service. So if anything different was recorded in the transcript, and I'll check that out, then I'll ask us to see what the tapes say and then put the transcript right if it's wrong. So there's no dilemma there. I didn't ask about the civilian organ, that is to say, the internal affairs civilian organ. Thank you. I asked about a security service or SIS, the military organ. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would -- I would object to these interruptions. I think that counsel's entitled to conduct the cross-examination. It affects all of us, and I don't think it's proper for someone to just simply stand up and clarify what they meant or what they did. We have a record. The record certainly can be pointed out. At the end of each day we do get a hard copy of that record. So if there is something that can be cleared. But I do think that for the purposes for, at least for the rest of us, this cross affects all of us, not just one individual. And I know that some of us were not terribly amused yesterday with some of the things that were going on yesterday. So I think Ms. Nozica is entitled to clarify the points that she's trying to clarify, because it does affect the rest of us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, may I just be allowed to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic, please. I'll try and clarify this matter. Ms. Nozica is putting a question to the witness, and she's dealing with the civilian police authority that was under -- subordinated to the Interior Ministry. She makes a reference to what you stated yesterday, and you take the floor to say that yesterday you never mentioned civilian security services but that you only mentioned the SIS as a military organ. Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, precisely what I wanted to say. Throughout that time yesterday we discussed SIS, and as far as I understood it, there was no misunderstanding or contention between myself and the witness in that regard. But might I just be allowed to say one additional sentence in view of the intervention made by my colleague Mr. Karnavas. I am going to put forward an objection of principle now, and that is that the rules of this Tribunal governing cross-examination determine that it refers to the topics raised duration the examination-in-chief, and exceptionally other relevant topics as well. Now, if in this courtroom cross-examination is allowed of cross-examination, so cross-examination of cross-examination, which was introduced once already by my colleague Ms. Nozica, then I would like to ask time for me to cross-examine subjects which other people raised in their cross-examination. And just one more remark. As far as words investigation is concerned, "istraga," or certain measures taken prior to an investigation, I endeavoured to use the term "investigacija," "investigation," which does not have a criminal legal connotation. So that the Trial Chamber receiving these -- the translation of the words, which is "investigation," should be quite clear on what we're talking about. And so for the Petkovic Defence, there's no doubt that the -- neither the organs of internal affairs or the SIS military police or anybody else from similar organs was authorised to conduct an investigation, "istraga," in the sense of criminal laws as provided for by the provisions of Herceg-Bosna, Republic of Croatia, et cetera. So that's the concept I wanted to explain. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could be heard just for a second because I do want to clarify the situation somewhat, and I apologise if I sound pedantic or if I'm -- or pedagogical when it comes to trial advocacy, but I do think that those folks who may come from a strictly continental tradition may not fully appreciate the fact that during the cross-examination it is not merely to confront evidence that came from the -- from the Prosecution, evidence that was elicited on direct examination, but when you have multiple parties, everything is fair game on cross-examination, and no one should be confused in this courtroom that, for instance, during the cross-examination, in rebutting the Prosecution's evidence in this instance, the burden could be -- or the blame can be shifted to another accused, and then that accused and his lawyer should simply sit there and take it. I'm not suggesting that's happening. All I'm saying is that you simply cannot suggest that you cannot cross-examine on cross-examination. The purpose of cross-examination is not only to challenge the evidence but is more properly to assist the Trial Chamber in having all of the facts in context, relevant as they may be, to assist the Trial Chamber at the end. That's the whole purpose. It's not a game. It's to allow you to have maximum amount of information that you can then discern and figure out what are the facts. So in any event, the other thing I wish to put in, and my -- I want to thank my colleague. We did mention this months ago about how Rule 90(H) 90(H) or 90(M), I can't remember which one it is. We are required to put our case to the witness. That's an English tradition, it's not a tradition that the Americans subscribe, but we do it anyways. But the basis for that is if something has come up during the testimony and you have a witness, you cannot simply forego the opportunity of putting that matter to the witness so that you can have an explanation from the witness, and then save it so you can bring it up at some other point, in other words, never giving the witness an opportunity to explain. So we do have an obligation to put our case to the witness, and we have that obligation. It's mandated by the rules. I know we've been rather lax a little bit in this court but we simply can't overlook that. I don't wish to engage in polemics. I don't wish to shift any blame or fix blame on anyone but I merely wish to state that everybody must understand that cross-examination, everything is fair game, and you can cross-examine on cross-examination, and that is proper within the rules. That's the nature of this tradition whether you like it or not. And I can be corrected by Mr. Scott or anyone else in the courtroom if I've spoken out of turn.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may be heard. I fully support what my colleague Karnavas has just said and I agree with every word of his, and I believe that it would be very good if every one of us is allowed to cross-examine after cross-examining. And I would like to remind you that I used that right only once after the cross-examination by the Defence of Mr. Coric, and I don't know if that happened ever again. And I believe that this is a rule that would allow the Trial Chamber to give as much information as possible, to understand our mutual relations and positions of certain Defence teams, which is all very relevant for this trial. I, however, believe that using that right which contributes to a fair trial cannot depend on the sequence of Defence teams that cross-examine, so that the second Defence team has -- is entitled to cross-examine upon the cross-examination of the first Defence team. If we allow that to become a principle, obviously we will have to allow the Defence teams that preceded to react with their additional cross-examination to the cross-examinations of the Defence teams that were next in the sequence. If the -- if this is not adopted, the cross-examination and the sequence of certain Defence teams will dictate the fairness of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Firstly, when it comes to the cross-examination, I would like to remind all parties that the Chamber rendered a decision on the 28th of April, 2006, and I would like to reiterate what was said. It is possible that when a question is put by a counsel of the accused that question can bring, on behalf of the accused, some requests for clarification, but in that case the Chamber must identify clearly the problem, and the problem in question, I did not identify the problem if there was one, because when Ms. Nozica started to put her question, Ms. Alaburic rose, and I did not understand very clearly what the problem was. So let's start from the beginning. Ms. Nozica, you have the floor. Put the question and we'll see where the problem lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as you have just said it yesterday, my colleague did not really dwell upon the affairs of the internal affairs. It was not my intention to get into that, and I believe that Mrs. Alaburic's intervention was premature. It was my intention to deal with the SIS, but I would like to say that certain authorities of the bodies of the internal affairs that were explained yesterday and that should have been taken over by the SIS were interpreted -- interpreted wrongly in legal terms, and I believe it is my duty to try and get the answers from this witness as to whether he was aware what was -- what he was talking about yesterday, what he was providing his answers. I don't have anything against the objections, but I would kindly ask my learned friends to complete a subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please clarify, and once again, it's a storm in a teacup.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My feeling exactly. I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to tell me how much time has had taken, because I'm trying to keep a very precise track of the time and the questions, so I would kindly ask you to tell me how much more time I have left.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My learned friend Ms. Alaburic asked you whether the interior affairs organs were in charge of collecting evidence that was needed by the Prosecutor to render a decision whether they would issue an indictment or reject any criminal charges, and you answered yes. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me go on, then. My colleague asked you what organ was mentioned in this article in the following terms: The authorised organs of the organ of security of the armed forces, and your answer was -- your answer was that this was the SIS. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well then. And finally a question was put to you along these lines: Can it be concluded that the SIS, in keeping with the rules and procedures as an organ in charge of investigations in criminal proceedings was in a position to decide whether to conduct an investigation or not, and your answer to that was yes. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And I repeat, sir, for your sake and for the sake of everybody in the courtroom, I know that you're not a legal expert, but I have to keep on insisting because of the answers that you provided to the questions yesterday. Do you know who or what were the authorities in keeping with the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina that was the -- that was adopted in this decree? What were the authorities of the organs of the internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you that I don't know precisely. I can own explain how I understood the whole thing, but I really don't know about the legal -- legal implications of all this. I'm not a legal expert, as you've just rightly said it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Pursuant to this decree as we have it before us, the internal affairs organs or the authorised persons of the security organ in the armed forces, could they conduct an investigation or was it within the exclusive purview of the prosecutor? You can say, "I don't know," "I know," "This is how it was." You can give us any answer that you believe are part of your knowledge. Everything is acceptable.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you that everything that happened and that was bad was left to the SIS and the military prosecutors. I don't know what each of them was competent for, and I don't know anything about their authorities. I believe that they knew exactly what their authorities were and that they followed that. I -- I can't tell you exactly what an on-site inspection was or what an investigation or where their authorities started or stopped.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You're saying that you don't know what the SIS was in charge of, whether it was an on-site inspection or investigation. But if we scroll down in the Croatian version. Article 27 is what I'm interested in. Can we please take a look at that article, Article 27 in the Croatian and English version, please. Article 27 and I'm going to read the article to you, says that: "The commander of a military unit or a military institution is obliged to take all necessary measures to prevent the offender, that if officially being prosecuted, from hiding or running away, to preserve all evidence of a crime, as well as the items that might become evidence, as well as to collect all information that could be used and useful for criminal proceedings." Witness, could you please answer, if you can? I believe that you can because you were a commander. Does it arise from this article that it was an obligation of the commander rather than of the SIS or the military prosecutor to collect all the information? And if I may add to that, the commander, in my view, was in a position to transfer his obligation to somebody else, but the decree recognises the commander as a person duty-bound to collect information. Would you say that this arises from this article?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I would add another sentence to that. A commander could not do it personally, on his own. A commander in the -- in the execution of this task will use the services at his disposal. A commander, as I was during that period of time, I had at my disposal the security service that in its terms, based on it's functional duties, had military -- the military police that could be used.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The obligations are yours, but you could charge, then task other services to perform the tasks. Those services were subordinated to you in military terms; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well, then. See how things are. "The commander of a military unit or a military institution is obliged to immediately forward the information listed in paragraph 1 of this Article to county military attorney or immediate commander." Which means that pursuant to this decree, this is another obligation that the commander had, i.e., to communicate to the county military prosecutor or the immediate commander. This is what arises from the decree, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please direct me to that particular paragraph in the article? I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's Article 27, paragraph 2. Can you see that the commander of the unit or institution is obliged to immediately forward the information to the county military attorney. Isn't that the fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's clarify one more thing from this article. When we're talking about military commanders, what could they do? Paragraph four says: "Military commander having the rank of a company commander, a person of the same or higher rank and an authorised official of the Internal Affairs, as well as the security organ or the military police may detain a military person in situations set out by the law on criminal proceedings in --" Would you agree with me that a military commander, the military police, the SIS, and the security organ have been put on a par here? They could all detain a person that committed a certain crime, am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If we sum up everything that I have just shown to you, would you agree with me that you had the obligation pursuant to this decree -- when I say you, I mean you and every other commander, and I'm not talking about any specific situation, is it true that you had the obligation to collect all the elements that were necessary in order to pass a decision whether a crime was committed and that you could have tasked some of your subordinates to carry out those tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In that case, you would have been duty-bound to check whether your subordinates carried out your orders in terms of the execution of the tasks that you charged them with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now just to corroborate these theoretical examples with practical examples, I would like to call up P 06137, which is the order issued by Mr. Petkovic, and I'm going to be using it in its part that corroborates the portions of Article 27 that I have just read out. The document is P 06137. I would like to call it up on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell me how much time have I got left while we're waiting for the document to be put on e-court?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes ago you had used one hour and six minutes, so I think it is 14 more minutes left, but the registrar will tell me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I'll speed up then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For the purposes of the explanation could you please look at items 2, 3, 4. The items 2, 3, and 4 of this order corroborate what we have just read out. It says here, "During the investigation involve the competent organs, and after the completion of the investigation send me a written report, and finally the aforementioned commanders will be directly responsible to me for the implementation of this order." This is what Mr. Petkovic does -- does. This is what you should have done in case of an investigation of a crime; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's now ignore, although this had to do with the collection of evidence that led to a final decision whether a crime was committed or not. An order was issued to you, the commander of the Bobovac Brigade, rather than to the SIS. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: With regard to the implementation of this order, you told us yesterday that in a telephone conversation Mr. Petkovic told you this: The SIS officials, Mr. Bandic and other members of the brigade SIS had either received instruction or would be receiving instructions as to how to proceed with regard to this order. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember their conversation with him, but we did not mention their further actions upon this order, because this was an order for me. We, rather, discussed their actions with regard to the overall situation with what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then we have to be more precise and say that you understood they would be given instructions as to how to proceed with regard to the entire inquiry as to what happened in Stupni Do. Is that the way we could put it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well then. Did they ever tell you about the instructions or orders that they had received? First of all, let me ask you whether your assistant for the SIS ever told you what kind of instructions had they received or what kind of orders they had received from anybody.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in that sense. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before your departure to Vares, did Mr. Bandic come to Kiseljak and, if so, when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were there for a couple of days before that. I can't be precise. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you say "they," who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean General Petkovic and Ivan Bandic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm now just asking you about Mr. Bandic. Why did he come to Kiseljak in the first place? What were his duties in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly why he came, because it wasn't his duty to inform me why he was coming, but I do know that from time to time he would be in the company of General Petkovic when he came up there, and that's a question that just General Petkovic and he could answer, the question of why.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, you don't know, so that's sufficient answer for me. You said that Mr. Bandic - and let's understand each other, he worked in the SIS administration, did he not? He wasn't subordinate to you - Wrote a report of the 8th and 15th of November, 1993, two reports, and for the transcript -- you don't have to look at the documents. You know them very well. You know what they're about. They're P 06519 and P 06671. So anybody who wishes to check them out can do so. And you just signed them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that Ivan Bandic wrote that. It was the service, Ivan Bandic's service, the SIS service, that wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you try and be precise, please. Please be as precise as possible. You said Ivan Bandic wrote it on one occasion, then you said you didn't know whether Ivan Bandic wrote it. So tell us what you know about that. Who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this report was compiled, according to what I know, by Zoran Duno who brought it -- brought the reports to me to be signed. And in the SIS, he was in the SIS, the service in which -- to which Ivan Bandic belonged too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Zoran Duno, wasn't he the assistant for SIS of the operation zone? You're a soldier. You know what the SIS administration in Mostar is and what the SIS officers are in the operation zone and in the operations group and what the assistant SIS in a brigade is. Now, since you say Mr. Zoran Duno brought you that and you say that for the first time, what post did Zoran Duno hold at the time, to the best of your recollections and we'll check it out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: By appointment he was in the brigade command. He was the assistant chief for security.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to explain? As before the war, he was a member of the civilian police force, and I think he had some duties in respect to investigations or worked in the crime department as far as I recall, or crime prevention department, then he was helping me in the Operative Group, and he would help out if something else needed to be done. So he wasn't in the Operative Group headquarters, but there are documents where he's referring to in that kind of way for him to be able to do his job.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. But as I understand you, he was not in the SIS administration in Mostar anywhere. He was either assistant for SIS in the brigade or he was assistant for SIS of OG 2. Now let's look at P 06841 where you are appointing him as assistant for SIS of OG 2 and it's your letter to Mate Boban. It will come up on e-court on your screen. Look at the very beginning. It's the Zvonko Duznovic document. You say you're doing this pursuant to orders from General Blaskic -- from Colonel Blaskic, and you say that investigation against Zvonko Duznovic should be conducted and assistant for SIS, that Zoran Duno, assistant for SIS of OG 2 should be involved. So it's the same period, the 24th of November, 1993. Is that how you referred to him in official documents? This document goes to Blaskic and the assistant for SIS of the military district of Vitez and it's addressed to Mate Boban too and in that document you say that Mr. Duno, you address him as assistant of SIS for OG 2, Operations Group 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Now, you're now telling us that this man Mr. Duno, who, de facto, was your assistant for SIS brought in those two documents for you to sign and you don't know who compiled them? Is that your final answer but you say you assume that someone else compiled them and not Zoran Duno.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think he worked on those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You mean Zoran Duno?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'd like to give an explanation here to avoid any misunderstanding. Yesterday I was explaining in what way the workers in the security service, those officers, what their duties and obligations were vis-a-vis the security service in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's all quite clear. They -- you said they were tied to Mostar. We'll see how they were connected to Mostar in due course, whether your information was correct or not, but just briefly now because I don't have much time, what you're saying is that you don't know that Mr. Bandic was involved in the writing of these documents at all. Is that your final answer? His name is mentioned a great deal in this courtroom. So that will be my last question on this matter. Do you deny, sir, that you don't know that Mr. Bandic or whether Mr. Bandic was the author of this and whether he was involved in the writing of those two documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say is that he was not the author because he brought them to me to sign. Whether he was involved or not I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, that's a slightly different answer than the one you gave a moment ago but it's an answer. My colleague says that it's not Judge Antonetti who says it. It's answer. Yes, it's been put right. And now my last question that I consider to be exceptionally important and I'll just deal with it briefly. Now, the investigation into Stupni Do, we'll see whether SIS conducted it or some of the brigade commanders, or the Prosecutor's office as the sole organ authorised to conduct an investigation. Now, please, sir, I'm going to show you a document. It will come up on e-court and it was one that Mrs. Alaburic showed you yesterday with her own number, it's the seventh one, 2D 00574 is the number. The seventh document from the top. Yes, 574, I'm sure you will recall that document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we see here that already on the 28th of October 1993 as it says here the deputy military prosecutor and prosecution in Travnik initiated proceedings to establish the facts as to what happened in Stupni Do. And in point 1, it says and the prosecutor refers to his authorisations to collect, gather the facts after gaining information that a crime had taken place that was being prosecuted in the line of duty, and Mrs. Alaburic, you cleared this up about what he was asking of the command of the Bobovac Brigade but I'd just like to add that in paragraph two he asks whether the soldiers of the Bobovac Brigade or Vares Brigade or members of some other military units in the area of responsibility of the Bobovac Brigade during the period from the 28th of October to the present day took part in perpetrating any kind of criminal acts. Now, is it logical that the prosecutor should be asking precisely the brigade -- the Bobovac Brigade commanders because allegedly or possibly something had happened in the area of his area of responsibility so he's asking the command of the Bobovac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So regardless of whether members of his own unit took part or somebody who came in from outside but it was all in his area of responsibility; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Finally at the end he says that this brigade commander is duty-bound to inform the prosecutor's office or district prosecutor about all this. I have been told that the transcript -- 28th of October somebody's saying that to me. It concerns line 6, line 6. The 28th of October. Yes. The 28th of October. That's what it says on the document. Well, I'm not quite clear what you mean. It says on the document the 28th of October. I'll look at it and put it right in due course if necessary. Anyway, do you know whether the commander of this unit acted upon this and did he indeed inform the prosecution subsequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir do you know that this means already on the 28th of October the military district prosecution had taken steps in conformity with its authorisation all steps and measures to investigate into what happened in Stupni Do? Does that follow from this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if that was all that needed to be done but based on this document we see that they did take these measures and steps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right, thank you. Just briefly let's look at the next document it is the eighth document from the top shown to you by Ms. Alaburic. It is 2D 00578.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your time is almost up. Please conclude very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, thank you. Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, we've seen the document before. I'd like to inform the Court inform the Trial Chamber or rather they noted that there were no statements attached to this document and that's true as you can see. The document is the one that we received from the Prosecution but I did not manage to find an attachment to the document. I looked for it under the number I was given but have not managed to find it so this will be the only document that will not be complete for objective and not subjective reasons. I'm using it because of the last sentence. Now, this is a document dated the 29th, the 29th of December, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We can see that the prosecution is still doing its work and still being sent documents, and in the last sentence the assistant commander for SIS brigade in Kiseljak, that's your assistant, is it not? Well, it's in your area of responsibility; right? Your OG, operations group, and he says, the last sentence: "If you consider that there is responsibility linked to this subject, the village of Stupni Do, then inform us thereof for us to be able to take further steps in the matter." Now, my final question, from this question and it's the last document we have about the investigation conducted by the prosecution that it is precisely your -- or, rather, the assistant for SIS of the brigade in Kiseljak contacted the prosecution's office on the 29th of December, they say this is what we have if you need anything further, ask us for it. Is that what follows on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And finally my question is this and it's a logical one: From the 28th of October - I don't know whether you know about this or not tell us if you don't - judging by the documents does it emerge that by the 28th of October that the district military prosecution in Travnik was involved became involved in the investigation; does that emerge from this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can say from the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From both documents, right? If you agree with me because this second document of the 29th of December is also sent to the same prosecution office; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you that completes my cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for letting me go beyond my time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why are you on your feet, Mr. Praljak? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Would Their Honours allow me to ask three questions to clarify whether the purchase of weapons from the Serbs was blackmail or not blackmail? I apologise, but I think that I should be given time to ask that, because this is what it's about. It's not marketing. You're not buying marmalade, jam and salad. It's a vital question, because without things like that would these people there have been -- would they have survived or would they have been killed? So is it blackmail or is it not blackmail?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure what the Court's inclinations are but I will add my objection to this. I really would like to have the opportunity to complete an a reasonable redirect. A huge amount of material has been covered. This is not proper, and I would ask the Trial Chamber to deny it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission just two sentences. I've gained the impression that from the cross-examination conducted by my colleague Ms. Nozica that it emerges that the Petkovic Defence intentionally erroneously presented certain provisions and decrees to the Court and asked for this witness's interpretation of them. I'd just like to draw your attention to the fact that from the provision and article that my colleague drew attention to about the military district prosecutor's office it emerges that the military district prosecutor's offices are -- have the right to require an investigation and that an investigation in the formal and legal sense and we wish -- that that is conducted by the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we have the argument later when the witness can be not in the courtroom and when the Prosecution can have its time, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I really don't want to respond to that. The transcript exists. The articles and provisions and decrees exist. The Court will decide. All I want to say is that I was correctly informed that I had made a mistake on page 64, line 6. It should not read the 28th of October but the 23rd of October. So I'd like to put that mistake right. And I think that the question just asked by Mr. Praljak was a key question of my cross-examination, and I think it would be a good idea if we could clear it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I object, and you know what? This goes back to the question of whether it's blackmail or not and I submit to the Chamber it's not even -- it's not even a substantial issue at this point in time. The Chamber's heard the evidence and not the characterisation of what Mr. Praljak wants to call it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judges have discussed the matter, and we decide not to allow Mr. Praljak to put questions to the witness about the so-called blackmail. This can only be a subjective matter. We as Judges have been submitted documents that testify to a number of events, weapons purchase, everything else. The rest is a matter of interpretation. When the time comes, Mr. Praljak, you'll be able to call your own witnesses if you want to bring that case before the Trial Chamber, but at the moment this is completely irrelevant for us. That's what I wanted to tell you, Mr. Praljak. What we're going to do now is that we're going to have a 20-minute break. Then we'll resume for redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. An additional bundle has been distributed. Let me alert everyone in the courtroom, as I already have with some counsel, that most of these, the vast majority of these exhibits have been used before, but in order to move as efficiently as possible as so that everyone doesn't have to be flipping back and forth between four or five different locations, hopefully all the documents have been put -- we will try to use if we have time -- will be in a single with possibly one or two exceptions of something that's just come up this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll be very brief. Just to give my learned friend a heads-up that it is your intention if the Prosecution deem it appropriate to put P 00185 to this witness, there will be an objection. Your Honour, I'm in your hands whether or not objection is taken now or perhaps it would be more appropriate, given my friend's comments that he may not put all the documents to the witness, that in the event he does put it to the witness at that point I will stand up and make the objection. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you've heard that we need to move rather crisply, please, so I'll ask your assistance in trying to answer my questions as directly as possible and you've been provided a new bundle of documents, hopefully everything that we're going to talk about I hope with possibly one or two exceptions will be in the new bundle and you won't have to go anywhere else. Let me go back to the topic of Stupni Do and Bogos Hill itself. Now, I believe in response to questions on cross-examination at some point you've used the term -- you said there was an "ABiH unit" in the village. And I would like to ask you -- further to build on that -- I'm trying to take this as quickly as possible. It was further developed at one point I think in response to one Defence counsel's question that the presence of armed Muslims in the village of Stupni Do was at the level of a reinforced platoon, and if I heard you correctly you said this would be something like approximately 36 soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I answered that question, but I can clarify what I meant if you wish me to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me just continue on and let me ask the particular questions and we'll see how it may fit into my questions to you. If you say there was a unit there, can you give us the name of that unit and the name of the commander of that unit, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we're talking about BiH unit, there was no unit there. These were locals that made up that unit and they defended their village. As for their numbers, they could have been considered a reinforced platoon, however, they could not be considered that in terms of the weaponry that they had at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I take it in the sense when you say could not have been a reinforced platoon in terms of the weaponry, they did not have the scope of weapons of a reinforced platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We agreed on that and that's part of the agreed facts, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me ask you this because there was some -- there were several references to some intelligence as I understood it, that possibly, possibly, there was something like 200 ABiH soldiers on their way or in possible transit to Stupni Do. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was such information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But not -- just so the evidence is very clear, sir, it's not your evidence that there were, in fact, 200 ABiH soldiers in the village of Stupni Do on the 23rd of October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The information was that they had been on their way from Sarajevo to Vares. I'm not claiming that they ever arrived or that that they entered Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry. If you can please turn quickly to Exhibit P 6 -- in your notebook it will just be 6026. In the -- toward the end of the first paragraph of this report which we've looked at a number of times, I believe, in the course of the last few days, you indicate there: The Bogos feature was taken by our forces and about 20 armed members of MOS, Muslim armed forces, defence forces, and some civilians remained in the village of Stupni Do. So can we take it from your answer, something about a reinforced platoon around -- perhaps as many as 36 soldiers and the report you made, in fact, at the time back in 1993 that number in -- the number of defenders in the village was somewhere perhaps between 20 and 36?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you've also mentioned -- I'm told that the transcript -- I said between 20 and 36 just so the record is accurate. Now, sir, you've also given information in response to Defence counsel's questions that Stupni Do was "fortified," and I wanted to ask you very specifically about the village itself. So I'm not asking you about Bogos Hill, leave Bogos Hill to one side. In the village of Stupni Do what specific fortifications were you aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see that on the footage of the Croatian TV of Kiseljak. One of the trenches was recorded, it was not in the village, however, it was on the brink of the village. However, according to the information that I received from the commanders that there were cases that cellars had been arranged for defence in some of the houses in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, that was basically where I was -- at least in part where I was heading, sir. A place in the cellar, arranged location in a cellar of a house, that would be primarily for defensive purposes or could you attack the town of Vares if you were sitting in a cellar in a house in Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was for sheltering civilians and for defence; however, from some positions, for example, the trench that I've mentioned, one could see Vares and one could use that trench to fire on Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the answer there is could have been used; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How far away is the village from Vares?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're talking about the settlement called Vares Majdan. As the crow flies it could have been some 300 to 500 metres or maybe up to a kilometre. It's difficult for me to tell from the position where I was. It could have been anything between 500 metres and a kilometre or maybe even two. The village is rather long, so it's very difficult to know what you mean when you're asking me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I just -- sir, can I ask you this: In the former Yugoslavia in 1992/1993, particularly in villages which had any proximity to fighting or the confrontation line, would it have been common on all sides, whether a Serb village, a Croat village, or Muslim villages for the people living there to perhaps have arranged some shelters or even a trench to defend the village if attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There were questions put to you Ms. Alaburic about the number of victims in Stupni Do, and in fact I think there was even possibly some suggestion that Muslims had smuggled bodies back into the village or perhaps that was where it was all leading. Can I ask you, please, to look at Exhibit 6146, 6146, please. This is a request from General Petkovic -- I'm sorry, my apologies. If you could go first to 6078, my apology, 6078. We'll come back to 6146 in just about 30 seconds, I hope. If you have 6078, sir, you see that that is a request for information on the 25th of October from General Petkovic asking, among other things, item 1: "Submit correct information on Stupni Do to me by 0900 hours, the number of MOS killed, the number of civilian casualties." Now, with that in mind if you then go to your 6146. In your item number 1 which appears to correspond to General Petkovic's item number 1, did you provide the following information about halfway through paragraph 1: "The majority of victims were burnt in the houses because the fighting progressed from house to house, area to area. According to the statement of the commanders who led the operation and you are acquainted with them, something like 25 to 30 balijas died and the number of civilians is a little less, between 20 and 25." Now, sir, if you could -- if we can agree that in the factual basis which you signed and told the former Trial Chamber was true, that approximately 37 people died as a result of the attack on Stupni Do, the numbers that you gave, in fact, on the response to General Petkovic's request were not terribly far off that number, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "yes," the answer I take it just so the record is clear, your numbers on that day were roughly consistent with what the ultimate numbers turned out to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, questions about -- a lot of questions about communications, lines of communication, whether General Petkovic, for example, could receive -- would have received a communication that had at the top of its heading "HVO Main Staff Mostar." And again, if you look at 6026 as an example, did -- and before we come back to that in a moment, is it correct to say, sir, that HVO Main Staff Mostar was the -- you might call it the regular duty post of both Mr. Praljak and Mr. Petkovic, just as your regular duty post was your headquarters in Kiseljak. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, for example, when you yourself sent your report 6026 on the 23rd of October, if you look at the letterhead, if you will, the format of the document, it starts with -- it says: "Command -- Vitez military district command of Operative Group 2 Kiseljak," that was the letterhead on the document you've sent but you've already told us that you were in Vares -- actually in Vares at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And isn't -- can you just tell the Judges, isn't that essentially the same thing that someone might have sent something to Petkovic or Praljak HVO Main Staff whether they were actually at that moment at that location or not, that was their normal address?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, a short objection. Here in front of the date it says that this was issued in Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That may be the case, but I'm referring to the information at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't that essentially the same thing, that was your duty post, and just like you might send a document from someplace else it would not be usual for you to use to indicate Kiseljak Operative Group 2 headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You've indicated that a man named Marinko Juricevic [sic], also known as Spiro was sent back to Kiseljak sometime around the 24th or 25th of October, I think you said at the same time as the bodies of the two killed HVO soldiers were sent back and Mr. Juricevic [sic] was sent back to give a report to Mr. Petkovic in Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you could turn to 6107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we move on to this particular exhibit, I have a question about the previous document, document 6026. It's a report you sent on the 23rd of October to Mr. Kordic, to Mr. Petkovic, and to Mr. Blaskic, as well as to the commander Bradara. I see here that we have a stamp. Please look at the B/C/S version of the document. There is a stamp from SIS dated 28th of October, 1993, number 5021. But in the report that you sent we don't have the names of the other addressees, archives, and so on and so forth. Is it the case that on the 28th of October, 1993, SIS found out, discovered, the contents of what -- the contents of your report? In other words, they found out that there had been an attack, that some people got killed, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see only that a stamp has been put here to show that the document was received. What happened to the document next and how it was treated, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, but what I wanted to point out was that the SIS in Mostar received the document on the 28th of October. Do you agree, because we have a stamp here with the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, if you could again look at 6107 and at the end of the first longer paragraph there are two shorter items. The second one says: "The burial was performed in a dignified matter," and this is a report by Mario Bradara on the 25th of October, 1993. Can you confirm that that would be the burial of the two HVO soldiers who had been killed on the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And so it was on that day that Mr. Juricevic went back to Kiseljak to report to General Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if we can turn quickly to Exhibit 6454, 6454, which is a presidential transcript of a meeting on the 5th of November, 1993, in Split. And -- sorry, I need to direct your attention quite quickly to page 59. We looked at this transcript the other day -- well, some days ago now -- actually starting on the bottom of page 58, the president says: "And who was in command of the Stupni Do operation?" "Pratkovic: M. EA led the forces to Vares while the commanders were in charge, it's a special-purpose unit from Kiseljak," et cetera. Then if we skip down a couple short paragraphs it says: "In the evening of the 24th Gavran and Duznovic -- Druznovic [phoen] were brought to Kiseljak on the order of M. EA and detained there. On the 25th I received the first report when we had two dead and 11 seriously wounded who were transported from Vares to Kiseljak, his name is Mr. Spiro." Now, is Spiro another name for Marinko Jurisevic [phoen]? Sorry, that one I can't get my mind around. Is that the same person that you sent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but just for the transcript I wish to draw attention to the fact that in one of your sentences you said that they were brought to Kiseljak. They were kept in Vares at that moment, but they had been taken in and later on they were transferred and I apologise, you were absolutely right -- yes, you're right, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think in the quotation the name of the witness comes up and probably it ought to be redacted also.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could go quickly in the bundle to a Defence exhibit that was shown to you, 4D 00844. Sir, I believe this document was shown to you yesterday, and just very quickly, it says: "We are asking you to provide three seats, Petkovic, Bandic, and Lucic" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I'm having some technical problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Bandic and Lucic on your helicopter flight tomorrow from Kiseljak to Split." Now, the Bandic that's referred to here, do you understand that to be the same Mr. Bandic, the SIS official, who had some involvement at least with the preparation of the reports on Stupni Do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. Lucic, the reference to Mr. Lucic, is that the same Vinko Lucic who we have heard about in the course of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So on that particular -- sometime around this time we heard that the flight might have been delayed and there wasn't the exact date, but around this time, after these events in Stupni Do, Petkovic, Bandic, and Lucic travelled together back to Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Petkovic and Bandic went, and I'm not sure about Lucic, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I would like you then next to go to 6963.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, to my surprise when I was looking at this document last night I found that it had not been -- at least this portion of it had not yet been translated. Obviously it will be. So I will need the -- I will need the assistance of the interpreters to put a couple questions to the witness about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you can look at the document. You indicated earlier that you understood some English, so it may assist you to also look at the document if it does. This is an UNPROFOR report dated the 30th of November, 1993, and this individual reports on two meetings with Mr. Lucic and Mr. Bandic. Now, in paragraph number 2 it indicates that Mr. Bandic introduced himself as a military lawyer. Can you just tell the Judges, did you know or was it correct that Mr. Bandic was a military lawyer? Or did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that moment I didn't know what his profession was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So you don't know if that statement -- when he introduced himself in such a way, you don't know if that was true or not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No -- no, you don't know whether it was true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what his profession was and I don't know how he introduced himself. I don't know whether he introduced himself this way or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. In item number 3, at the end of item number 3 -- paragraph number 3 -- well, in that paragraph Mr. Bandic talks about Stupni Do and says, Well, it was a military setting after all. And he says at the end of that -- or is attributed to him. "He agreed, however, that this couldn't justify the things that had happened in the village." And I take it, sir, from your guilty plea you agree with that assessment?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honours, with your leave I would kindly ask my learned friend from the Prosecution what do his questions arise from? Both Ms. Alaburic and I mentioned Bandic, but we never denied for one single moment that he was there and we never asked the witness or challenged the things that the Prosecutor is now raising. My question was whether Mr. Bandic drafted documents that the witness said that he had. I didn't challenge that. I asked the witness when he arrived in Kiseljak, and from the document that Mrs. Alaburic showed to the witness we saw when he left to Kiseljak. And for the possible contacts with the representatives of the international organizations, this was not a topic of cross-examination. That's why I don't see the foundation to ask these questions in the course of re-direct. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, to respond briefly, it's the Prosecution case, as I'm sure the Judges must know by now, that there was a massive cover-up concerning the crimes committed at Stupni Do, reaching to the very top of the HVO government, and including, in fact, people in Zagreb. Now -- and of course the Defence contest that and in cross-examination a number of questions were put to the witness about -- in generally trying to disprove that there was a cover-up. This Mr. Bandic, by all indications, was extensively involved in these matters, and I wanted to put to this witness in response to the questions raised during cross-examination whether Mr. Bandic had it right or whether he was intentionally, or unintentionally perhaps, also falsely representing the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may be heard and I certainly don't want to disrupt the proceedings, but I don't think it's contested. I think the evidence is rather clear from the direct examination and it wasn't contested on the cross that this particular gentleman has lied, as lied repeatedly about his identity, about what he has done, that he was hiding, that he is a master of deceit and lies and I think that has been proven and I don't think -- so that's not challenged. I think documents were presented to show the gentleman was told what to do and when to do it and how to do it. So now if there is something to contradict what came in through the cross-examination, I would like to know concretely what it is that the Prosecution is trying to do. If they want to merely bolster and supplement their direct examination, I think it's improper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My questions, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. I will try to summarize the problem. On the one hand the Prosecution would like to put a question to the witness arising from this document. We had seen this document already because the document was already presented through another witness. Therefore, the Judges know this document very well. Secondly, the Defence wanted to establish by putting their questions that there had not been no manipulations to hide or dissimulate, there was no cover-up, and the Prosecutor gives a contrary opinion and he wishes to verify this by putting a question to the witness, by quoting the third paragraph of this document in which Mr. Bandic states officially to the UNPROFOR that things happened in the village indeed. So apparently Mr. Bandic is not trying to cover anything up. Once again, this is a storm in a teacup. Please put your question, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I would just like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to the Prosecutor's question on page 12, lines 11 and 12. The Prosecutor says: "Sir, you have admitted that in your plea agreement." I don't think this should be allowed by way of suggesting the witness's answer. If that is allowed, then we should have been given the plea agreement and all the documents that entered into that, and we could have ended this cross-examination very quickly. Everything else that has been presented in the courtroom in the meantime have been given a different face. He has not denied that he has pleaded guilty but he should not be kept on suggesting to him all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, that's another problem. Ms. Nozica is perfectly right, Mr. Scott. The witness only recognised in the document that he signed with the Prosecutor, the plea agreement, there are some paragraphs that he recognised and there are exactly - and I'm leafing through - there are 43 paragraphs exactly. So you are alluding to what paragraph exactly? And then I will hand the floor to Mr. Kovacic. What is the paragraph that you are evoking when you are talking about the factual basis? What are the paragraphs exactly that you would like to invoke?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will have to get it out again, Your Honour. I would move on to another question, forget item number 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please put another question. Mr. Kovacic and then the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, a technical question in order to avoid any subsequent misunderstandings and difficulties. Once we read the transcript and the documents, document 5639 that Prosecutor is dwelling upon according to the ERN number is one and the same document, the ERN numbers are in sequence from 288 to 292 but we are talking about two documents, even their internal numbers and those are the numbers of the author 241101 in the upper right-hand corner, these are not the same documents. And if we want to refer to those documents later and if the document refers in question the first one that has five items, item 1 is not the same as item 3 in the second document under the same number, which has 21 items. I just wanted to hear precisely what document is being referred to because later on we might all have -- face problems in dealing with these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Fine. Yes, Witness, you wanted to say something. What was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I appreciate the lawyers' rights to use various methods in order to put pressure on the witness and to obtain information that is in the interests of their case; however, the gentleman on the left-hand side who portrayed me as a liar, I believe that this insults my dignity and I cannot not react to those words. About who did what and how people behaved is up to the Chamber to decide, and then we will see who was a liar, who was a hypocrite, who had thick skin, and I would kindly ask the other lawyers to refrain from using the qualifications that insult my dignity and I think I have every right to feel insulted and hurt at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... In the interests of time because time is very precious as we all know. Sir, if I can ask you to move on to paragraph number 4 of the same document that we were looking at it says there: "I asked Mr. Bandic what happened with Mr. EA, the commander of the unit that committed the war crimes. I was told that he was revoked but that he was given some advisory jobs." Just to confirm again, sir, you had not been revoked as at that time; correct? You were still in your same position commanding exactly the same forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And at the end the statement is attributed to Mr. Bandic it says: "According to Mr. Bandic it wasn't sure whether Mr. EA was aware of the attack on the village." Now, sir, you told us that in fact on the morning of the 23rd of October you were at a location nearby the village at the time when the attack was going on -- or at least the portion on Bogos Hill; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really have to stand up again, and I apologise to my learned friend. No -- at no point during the cross-examination did anybody put questions to this witness as to whether he -- when it came to what he knew about what had happened in Stupni Do had ever told Mr. Bandic about that. So this Prosecutor's question is a misimplication that what the witness knew Mr. Bandic knew as well. First of all, there was no words said about that in cross-examination, and second of all, this question does not have a valid foundation because we know what the witness knows but we don't know what Mr. Bandic knew about these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, very briefly, again, it's the Prosecution's case - and we will -- that's what we will ultimately argue - that Mr. Bandic also was a member of the cover-up and that if Mr. Bandic didn't know by the end of November, a month later, after supposedly an investigation had been conducted, if he didn't know that Mr. -- Witness EA had not been in the village, he wasn't even aware of the attack on that day, I leave it to the Chamber to ultimately draw its own inferences about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, forgive me. Of course my learned friend who I have the greatest of respect for, Mr. Scott, is perfectly entitled to put his case. No objection is taken to that. It's simply objected that this is the inappropriate point of this witness's testimony to put his case. It must arise -- there must be some discipline in the courtroom, with the greatest of respect, Your Honour, and my learned friend, lead counsel, is quite correct. It must -- cross-examination must arise -- re-examination must arise out of cross-examination, and this re-examination does not arise out of any cross-examination put forward by the counsel for the accused. And for that reason, Your Honours, it should be -- it should be circumscribed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm moving on in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's best to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Because now we're just going in circles and we're definitely not contributing to the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Again, technical point, the witness's name has been mentioned several times and that should be redacted. You're a recidivist, Mr. Scott, I can understand, but I have to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I do appreciate that. The problem is when I'm referring to a document I don't think the document refers to the fact that whether a man is a witness in the courtroom; it's a historical document that gives a report, but nonetheless I understand the sensitivity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if we could move on then to Exhibit 7460. Again, many questions have been asked about how the investigation was conducted, what contacts, if any, you were having with General Petkovic during this time. And this appears to be a document from Viktor Andric dated the 1st of January, 1994, to General Petkovic. And, among other things, I want to direct your attention, please, to the fourth bullet item, so to speak, where it says: "We kindly request that you remove Marinko Ljoljo's written statement from the report of Stupni Do dated 15 November 1993 since it is not signed. We enclose a somewhat altered and signed statement of the aforementioned. The statement needs to be removed so it would not contradict the present statement and processing of the case according to your latest instruction." So my question: Is it correct, sir, that throughout this time while this investigation was ongoing, you were continuing to have communications with General Petkovic on the subject and the conduct of the investigation, including sending witness statements -- alleged witness statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I'd been asked to forward the statement, I would have done it or what -- whatever else that had to do something with those actions and activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I would like to turn to the topic of the facts you'd said you received, and you mentioned this both in direct examination and again in questions in cross-examination. The facts and conversations you say you had with Mr. Perica Jukic in approximately mid-November of 1993. When I reviewed your testimony you'd said you'd spoken to Mr. Jukic, two or three variants or scenarios were outlined to you concerning your situation, but it's not clear from the testimony that I reviewed whether you had fully explained what those two or three variants or scenarios were. Can you assist us in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the scenarios was that they would put me under investigation fictitiously, even to put me in prison for a while and to present those things to the international community as if the investigation had been carried out. Another scenario was to send me out of Vakuf to Kiseljak and engage me there or even somewhere else so that I could still be in touch with the area of Kiseljak and Central Bosnia. I can't remember the other scenarios. There were several to which I said, Please, don't make me decide on what should be done. You decide and tell me what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, a moment ago on line 23 you said -- or perhaps 21 he's talking about send me out of Vakuf to Kiseljak, did you mean the opposite, to be sent out of the Kiseljak area and to operate instead in the area of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was one of the scenarios. I was supposed to participate in the corridor operation from Gornji Vakuf to Central Bosnia or another solution had to be sought for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber -- can you confirm again, how long or when was it after your communications with Mr. Jukic that the idea of using a new name and identity, which ultimately became Viktor Andric, when was that scenario presented to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you the exact time, it may have been 15 days, 10 days, 20 days or a month even later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. We'll leave it at that for now. Sir, you were asked the questions -- you were asked several questions today, in fact, and there was some exchange between -- to the Defence counsel about your responsibilities and duties as a commander in terms of the -- what happened at Stupni Do and in Vares. But I don't -- I'm not sure the next question was actually put to you which is the question I want to follow up. If those, in fact, were your duties, if I heard your testimony, you agreed with counsel that in fact as a commander those were your duties, why didn't you do those things? Why didn't you carry those duties out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I had received a message from General Petkovic and because in my conversation with him he explained to me that I was not to deal with that any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Just on one -- just taking -- there's some loose-end items that I need to deal with quite quickly. In an -- if we could have the assistance of e-court because it only came up later this morning. If we could have Exhibit P 07757, which is one of the documents used today. And, sir, I'm going to have to ask you in this instance, it's not in the new bundle, if you could look at 7757, that was a document that was put to you in connection with a reward that was being paid to the special-purpose unit Maturice, if we can have that. And, sir, I think I asked you this on direct, but in light of the questions that were put to you and the way the document was used during cross-examination, can you confirm to the Judges this was a special reward, I think the word "reward" is even used somewhere, contribution, special-purpose units, was this part of the regular salary that was being paid to the units at this time or was this a special financial reward that was being given to the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a special financial compensation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to turn -- go back to Stupni Do and specifically -- specifically the Bobovac Brigade. Now, can you tell us -- well, first of all, I don't want there to be left any impression with the Chamber unless you indeed say it's the corrected impression, but you talked about the fighting in Bogos Hill and then there was some part of your testimony which might, might be interpreted to say there was really the fighting in Bogos Hill and then it kind of accidentally spilled over into Stupni Do. And can I just ask you to confirm, sir, when things kicked off on the 23rd -- the morning of the 23rd of October, the plan was to attack Stupni Do, correct, to take over the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a plan to take the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in that regard, what was the specific role of the Bobovac Brigade to be, if any, in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should have been the logistical and every other support to the special units that were supposed to take over the area. And after those units left the area after the mission was completed, the brigade was supposed to take over the area, to keep it and use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. I'm again -- let me focus now on specifically the 23rd of October, the actual taking over of the village that you just made reference to a moment ago. Apart from logistical support, apart from being in the background, perhaps providing broader security in the area, tell the Judges, please, as specifically as possible: Did the Bobovac Brigade or any members of that brigade have specific combat duties in the operations in and around the village itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Witness. The Prosecutor put to you that the plan was to attack the village. Very well. This is what you confirmed as well. But I would like to ask you a question that is a military one. According to you, there were approximately 30 villagers, fighters, who were defending this village. How can you explain then, then when you had special units you did not think of a commando operation that was executed during the night to take the village during the night, for instance, without all these shootings going on. Is that not a military technique to take control of a village by using a commando action during the night while everybody is sleeping?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, people who were defending the village were deployed on positions around the village. They had some sort of trenches there and they could follow every movement by day and by night, so no such action was possible. The only that was possible was the thing that had been agreed, to take Bogos Hill first and to put the defenders of the village into a rather unfavourable position, to make them see that there was an area behind their backs that they couldn't defend and to force them to leave the village. However, this scenario fell through because of the different development of events that I have described. And let me add to this, when the Prosecutor is asking me about Stupni Do and Bogos, I can tell you that the special units participated in that. But next to them the Bobovac Brigade was deployed defending Pajtov Han and they were in close contact and there were military operations going on there as well, but those were defence operations. The HVO was engaged in defence in those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where was Mijo Bozic and what was his position or function on the 21st of October, 1993, I'm going back a day or two before the actual operation?
